_about: Real published circuits, read from their sources on 2026-10-08, to check Circuit OS against. Every value below is what the SOURCE states or what its schematic netlist contains; anything the source does not state is listed under `assumed`. Read by the agent, not yet verified by a person (the same standing as data/figures.py records before scripts/verify_figures.py). Evidence classes: eagle-netlist (parsed from the vendor's own EAGLE .sch, connectivity machine-read) > standard-text / app-note-text / datasheet-figure (read from the document) > tutorial-text (a vendor's teaching page). The AM2302-labelled copy of the Aosong datasheet carries its connection diagram too small to read; the SparkFun-hosted DHT22 copy is legible and is the one cited.

schema.elements: R: {id, kind:'R', a, b, ohm, tol} · C: {id, kind:'C', a, b, farad, tol, dc:false} · SRC: {id, kind:'V', a, b:'0', volts_ref:'supply'} · LED: {id, kind:'LED', a, b:'0', led}
schema.request: the form Circuit OS would be asked for the same job: {function, fields}
schema.assumed: numbers the source did not give, and what they were taken as

red_0805.basis: assumed: the same red 0805 figures the project tabulates for its own LED (Würth 150080RS75000, data/component_constraints.py); the references name only 'RED 0805'

green_0603.basis: assumed: a conventional green 0603 chip LED; the reference names only 'Green 0603'

designs.title: Modbus over Serial Line V1.02 — polarized pair, 150 Ω terminations at both ends (range ends 450 Ω and 650 Ω)

source.doc: MODBUS over serial line specification and implementation guide V1.02, Modbus-IDA, 20 Dec 2006

designs.states: pull-up to 5 V on D1 and pull-down to common on D0, each between 450 Ω and 650 Ω, polarization at ONE location only; termination 'may be a 150 ohms value (0.5 W) resistor' at each of the two ends

assumed.tolerance: the spec gives no resistor tolerance; taken as 1%
assumed.labelling: A and B are named as MAX485/TI do (the receiver reads high for V_A − V_B ≥ 200 mV); Modbus calls the pulled-up line D1 and the pulled-down line D0. The idle differential has the same magnitude under either naming.

designs.title: TI RS-485 Design Guide — external idle-bus failsafe biasing (Fig. 7-1): RB 523 Ω ×2, RT 120 Ω at each end

source.doc: SLLA272D The RS-485 Design Guide, TI, Feb 2008 rev. May 2021

designs.states: for V_bus,min = 4.75 V (5 V − 5 %), V_AB = 0.25 V (200 mV threshold + 50 mV noise) and Z0 = 120 Ω, R_B = 528 Ω; two 523 Ω resistors are used with R_T = 120 Ω

assumed.tolerance: the guide gives none; taken as 1%
assumed.two_terminations: Fig. 7-1 shows R_T at each end of the bus

designs.title: SparkFun RS-485 Breakout — transceiver U2, no bias network, 220 Ω across A–B

source.where: parts R3, R4, C3, LED3, U2; nets A, B, RTS, VCC

designs.states: net A = U2.A, JP2.2, JP3.2, R4.1, JP4.8; net B = U2.B, JP2.3, JP3.3, R4.2, JP4.7; R4 value attribute '220' (device name '22OHM…'); no resistor from A or B to VCC or GND; DE and /RE tied to RTS

assumed.tolerance: R4 is a 1/10 W 1 % 0603 per its device name
assumed.supply: the breakout is a 3.3 V part (SparkFun product page); the schematic names only 'VCC'

designs.notes: R4's value attribute (220) and its device name (22OHM) disagree in the schematic; a community thread asks whether it should be 120 Ω. Taken as 220 Ω, the value attribute.

designs.title: Adafruit Feather M0 Basic — D13 LED: GPIO → 2.2 kΩ → red 0805 LED

source.where: net D13 = JP3.4, R7.1, U$4.PA17; net N$2 = L.A, R7.2; L.C on GND; R7 value '2.2K', L value 'RED' 0805

assumed.pin_resistance_ohm: the SAMD21 output resistance is not in the schematic; 40 Ω taken (negligible against 2.2 kΩ)

designs.title: SparkFun RS-485 Breakout — RTS line → 330 Ω → green 0603 LED

source.where: net N$4 = R3.1, LED3.A; net RTS = U2.DE, U2./RE, JP9.4, R3.2; LED3.C on GND; R3 '330', LED3 'Green' 0603

assumed.drive_level: RTS is the host's logic level; taken 3.3 V to match the SP3485-class transceiver on the board

designs.title: Adafruit Feather M0 Basic — battery monitor: VBAT → 100 kΩ → D9/A7 → 100 kΩ → GND

source.where: net VBAT includes R3.1; net D9 = JP3.8, R3.2, R6.1, U$4.PA07; R6.2 on GND; R3 '100k', R6 '100K'

assumed.supply_range: a single-cell Li-Po, 3.2–4.2 V (Adafruit's own description of the board); the schematic names only 'VBAT'

designs.title: SparkFun Logic Levels tutorial — 5 V → 3.3 V with 1 kΩ and 2 kΩ

source.doc: SparkFun learn: Logic Levels, 'Shifting Logic Levels'
source.where: 'You can use a simple voltage divider (like a 1KΩ and a 2KΩ) to knock down 5 V signals to 3.3 V levels'

assumed.orientation: the page does not say which resistor is on top; 1 kΩ on the input side is the only one that gives about 3.3 V

designs.title: Aosong DHT22 datasheet — electrical connection diagram: MCU DATA with a 5K pull-up to VDD

source.where: §5 Electrical connection diagram (a figure; the label reads '5K'); §6(1) supply 3.3–6 V, 100 nF between VDD and GND

assumed.tolerance: the figure shows no tolerance; taken 5 %
assumed.value: the figure's '5K'; the AM2302 manual's 'typical 5.1 kΩ' is how the project's own generator cites it

designs.title: Adafruit DHT guide — 10 kΩ between VCC and the data pin

source.doc: Adafruit Learn: DHT Humidity Sensing on Arduino, 'Connecting to a DHTxx Sensor'
source.where: 'a 10 Kohm resistor between VCC and the data pin'; power 3.3–5 V

designs.title: NXP AN14520 — PWM DAC output filter: 4.7 kΩ and 0.1 µF on a 3.3 V, 40 kHz PWM

source.doc: NXP AN14520 General MCU PWM DAC Application, Rev. 1.1, 22 April 2025
source.where: §2.2 Design of parameters: 'R = 4.7 K and C = 0.1 µF'; §2.1: settling about 2.86 ms

assumed.tolerance: the note gives none; R 1 %, C 10 %

designs.title: Espressif hardware design guidelines — RC delay on the EN (CHIP_PU) pin: 10 kΩ and 1 µF

source.doc: ESP Hardware Design Guidelines (ESP32), Schematic checklist
source.where: Chip Power-up and Reset Timing: 'The recommended setting for the RC delay circuit is usually R = 10 kΩ and C = 1 µF.'

assumed.use: a power-up delay, not a signal filter — included because it is a published RC low-pass with explicit values
